title: RHOA lactylation at oncogenic hotspots promotes oncogenic activity and protein stabilization.
authors: Ma, Chenglong; Liao, Ruocen; Chen, Xingyu; Cao, Qianhua; Deng, Xinyue; Dai, Zhijun; Dong, Chenfang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究RHOA蛋白乳酸化修饰对肿瘤活性的影响，核心是蛋白质翻译后修饰与肿瘤信号，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或相关AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aberrant RHOA activation drives tumor progression, yet regulatory mechanisms beyond genetic mutations remain poorly defined. Lactylation, a lactate-derived post-translational modification, links metabolic reprogramming to oncogenesis, but its functional mimicry of genetic mutations is unexplored. This study investigates RHOA lactylation at oncogenic hotspots and its role as an "epi-mutation" system. METHODS: RHOA lactylation were identified by pan-lysine lactylation (Kla) antibody-based mass spectrometry. Site-specific lactylation was achieved using an orthogonal Mb-Pyl Kla-RS/Pyl-tRNA pair to incorporate lactyl-lysine at K118/K162 in recombinant RHOA, validated by immunoblotting and fluorescence. Molecular dynamics simulations (AlphaFold 3, BIOVIA DS) analyzed GTPase activity and hydrogen-bond networks. RHOA activity was assessed via ROCK2-RBD pull-down and GTPase assays. Ubiquitination and protein stability were examined using cycloheximide chase and K48/K63-ubiquitin mutants. In vitro lactylation/delactylation assays with PCAF/HDAC3 defined enzyme specificity. In vitro/in vivo functional studies used migration/invasion assays and xenograft models. Clinical relevance was evaluated in breast cancer tissues and survival databases. RESULTS: We identify lactylation of RHOA at oncogenic mutation hotspots K118 and K162, mediated by the lactate-PCAF/HDAC3 axis. Mechanistically, K118 lactylation constitutively activates RHOA by impairing intrinsic GTPase activity, whereas K162 lactylation stabilizes RHOA protein by competitively antagonizing protein ubiquitination, with USP9X further enhancing stability through deubiquitination. Functionally, RHOA lactylation promotes tumor cell migration, invasion and metastasis. Clinically, RHOA lactylation is elevated in breast tumors versus adjacent tissues. Notably, targeting lactate production (LDHA inhibitor: sodium oxamate) synergized with RHOA-pathway inhibition (ROCK inhibitor: Y-27632) to suppress tumor progression. By employing a site-specific lactylation system, we further identify that lactylation mimics oncogenic mutations by enhancing both RHOA activity and stability, thus proposing that lactylation at mutation-prone sites represents a reversible "epi-mutation" system that recapitulates genetic mutation effects. CONCLUSIONS: RHOA lactylation at K118 (activation) and K162 (stabilization) orchestrated by the PCAF/HDAC3 enzymatic axis, enables constitutive oncogenic signaling to fuel tumor progression. Crucially, we redefine that lactylation at mutation-prone sites functions as a reversible "epi-mutation" system, where metabolic modification dynamically recapitulates oncogenic mutation effects, challenging the genetic/epigenetic dichotomy in oncology and revealing dual targeting of lactylation and canonical RHOA pathways as a potential therapeutic strategy.
abstract_zh: 背景：RHOA的异常激活驱动肿瘤进展，然而除基因突变外的调控机制仍不明确。乳酸化（lactylation）是一种源自乳酸翻译后修饰，将代谢重编程与肿瘤发生联系起来，但其对基因突变的功能模拟尚未被探索。本研究探讨RHOA在致癌热点位点的乳酸化及其作为“表观突变”系统的作用。方法：通过基于泛赖氨酸乳酸化（Kla）抗体的质谱鉴定RHOA乳酸化。利用正交Mb-Pyl Kla-RS/Pyl-tRNA对在重组RHOA的K118/K162位点特异性掺入乳酸化赖氨酸，实现位点特异性乳酸化，并通过免疫印迹和荧光验证。分子动力学模拟（AlphaFold 3、BIOVIA DS）分析GTPase活性和氢键网络。通过ROCK2-RBD下拉和GTPase实验评估RHOA活性。使用环己酰亚胺追踪和K48/K63-泛素突变体检测泛素化和蛋白稳定性。使用PCAF/HDAC3进行体外乳酸化/去乳酸化实验，确定酶特异性。体外/体内功能研究采用迁移/侵袭实验和异种移植模型。临床相关性在乳腺癌组织和生存数据库中评估。结果：我们鉴定出RHOA在致癌突变热点K118和K162位点的乳酸化，由乳酸-PCAF/HDAC3轴介导。机制上，K118乳酸化通过损害内在GTPase活性组成性激活RHOA，而K162乳酸化通过竞争性拮抗蛋白泛素化稳定RHOA蛋白，USP9X通过去泛素化进一步增强其稳定性。功能上，RHOA乳酸化促进肿瘤细胞迁移、侵袭和转移。临床上，与癌旁组织相比，乳腺肿瘤中RHOA乳酸化水平升高。值得注意的是，靶向乳酸产生（LDHA抑制剂：草酸钠）与RHOA通路抑制（ROCK抑制剂：Y-27632）协同作用，抑制肿瘤进展。通过采用位点特异性乳酸化系统，我们进一步发现乳酸化通过增强RHOA活性和稳定性模拟致癌突变，从而提出突变易发位点的乳酸化代表一种可逆的“表观突变”系统，重现基因突变效应。结论：由PCAF/HDAC3酶轴协调的RHOA在K118（激活）和K162（稳定）位点的乳酸化，能够实现组成性致癌信号传导，促进肿瘤进展。关键的是，我们重新定义突变易发位点的乳酸化作为可逆的“表观突变”系统，其中代谢修饰动态重现致癌突变效应，挑战肿瘤学中遗传/表观遗传的二分法，并揭示双重靶向乳酸化和经典RHOA通路作为潜在治疗策略。
